policy.artifact_rule: for each src/**/*.ts the sibling .js file is the emitted build artifact; it is never hand-edited and is byte-compared by tests/unit/migration/toolchain.test.js
policy.runtime_rule: JavaScript compatibility entries keep working: root index.js, bin/selfcheck.js, and not-yet-migrated src/**/*.js modules load the emitted .js artifacts with no loader change and no Node type stripping

phases.name: pure control
phases.deferred_reason: The remaining large algorithm modules (graph/plan/execute/kernel) are still JavaScript compatibility entries in this increment: converting them in one change would be a big-bang rewrite of the security-critical execution path, which TS-05 forbids. They keep their JSDoc boundary types and are guarded by the unchanged 516-test baseline; a follow-up increment converts them one module per green step. Their imports of the migrated protocol/control modules resolve the emitted .js artifacts, so the migration already changed no runtime path.

phases.name: market-stage evidence sidecars (t5 handoff)
phases.handoff_reason: t5 converted its new modules to TypeScript source + emitted .js before handoff and verified byte freshness; listed here so the migration freshness gate covers them too. Semantics remain fail-closed (providers development-only/blocked; no KMS/HSM/WORM/TSA trust root).

phases.name: protocol/adapters/worker/reports/CLI/plugin
phases.pending_reason: Not started in this increment; these modules remain JavaScript compatibility entries. New market-stage modules added by t4/t5/t6/t7 are authored as TypeScript from day one and are type-gated by the same root tsc run; this phase tracks only the pre-existing L1 baseline modules.

new_code_rule: Every module created after this migration starts as src/**/*.ts and is emitted to its sibling .js; allowJs/checkJs is only a bridge for the pre-existing L1 baseline, never a home for new code.
